methodology.study_design: diagnostic analysis of institutional barriers in marine governance for floating offshore wind in the UK Celtic Sea
methodology.sample_description: UK Celtic Sea floating offshore wind governance context; multiple actors including policymakers, regulators, industry representatives, and marine users

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Article addresses marine/institutional governance of floating offshore wind using institutional theory; it does not study LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance in regulated AI deployments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text repeatedly discusses governance, regulation, trust, legitimacy, and institutional barriers, these terms refer to marine policy and offshore renewable energy governance in the Celtic Sea, not to governance of LLM-based conversational systems. Python triage appears to be a keyword false positive. No evidence in the provided text links the study to AI, LLMs, or conversational technologies.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is clear from title, abstract, keywords, and introduction; technology mismatch is unambiguous in supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects only signals visible in the excerpt. The study appears internally coherent for marine institutional governance, but transferability to conversational LLM governance is very low. Sampling, data collection, analysis details, and limitations are not sufficiently described in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: For the review scope on conversational governance in LLM systems, relevance is very low because the article concerns marine governance of floating wind, not AI systems. Coherence within its own domain appears moderate from the abstract, but adequacy and methodological detail are unclear from the excerpt provided.

coding.theme: Institutional barriers in marine governance for offshore renewable energy
coding.subtheme: Fragmented governance landscape for floating wind in the UK Celtic Sea

synthesis.main_claim: Governance challenges for floating offshore wind in the UK Celtic Sea arise from systemic and synergistic institutional barriers rooted in institutional attributes that regulate roles, structure networks, and distribute power, rather than from isolated policy failures.
synthesis.contribution: Links institutional barriers in marine governance to underlying institutional attributes and argues for reconfigured marine governance arrangements emphasizing reflexivity, adaptability, and collaborative learning.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance; may serve only as distant contextual background on generic institutional governance language, but not recommended for synthesis due to domain and technology mismatch.
